title: Noah Lyles sets best-ever 150m time, beats Gout Gout in Czech Republic
content:
Noah Lyles has beaten Australian teenage sprinting sensation Gout Gout over 150m in Ostrava, Czech Republic, running a best-ever time of 14.67s.

Lyles, racing out of lane seven, one outside Gout, was victorious by one tenth of a second over South Africa’s Sinesipho Dambile (14.78s). Gout came third and also dipped under the 15-second barrier (14.96s) in still conditions.

It is, technically, the best run ever for this distance as a specific race — Lyles bettered the 14.92s time that Jamaica’s Kishane Thompson ran this April. However, World Athletics, the sport’s governing body, do not recognise the event for world record purposes.

Usain Bolt hit the 150m mark at 14.44s en route to his 19.19s 200m world record at the 2009 World Championships. Lyles has repeatedly split 14.70s for the distance when racing half a lap on the track, and therefore running the bend. He’s also second on the all-time list for 150m in a straight line, behind Bolt.

Significantly, this is Lyles’ seventh win of the calendar year and a first competitive outing for him against Gout, 18, who is a training partner of his under coach Lance Brauman in Florida.

“It was about time. The world record was quite slow,” Lyles told reporters after. “This feeling (to become the fastest in the world) — it is nothing new. I said I could have a better turn. It is very hard to get used to running in a staggered 150 start.”

He had the slowest reaction time in the field but, in classic Lyles fashion, won the race with his phenomenal top-end speed.

“All in all, I think that it was really good,” added the five-time world champion and 2024 Olympic 100m gold medallist.

Gout redeemed himself after a sixth-place finish on his Diamond League debut last week, when he ran 20.60s for 200m in Oslo. Here, like in Norway, he started slowly — accelerating on the bend does not suit his long legs and mechanics — and closed on the field along the home straight. The teenager will go to world under-20s this summer in Eugene, Oregon, while Lyles is expected to compete at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest, Hungary, in mid-September.

Elsewhere in Ostrava, Audrey Werro made it 10 wins from 12 races over 800m in 2026. The Swiss ran a meet-record time of 1:54.45s, her second-quickest ever and the eighth-fastest of all time.

They split 55.83s at halfway and Werro won by over two seconds. Femke Broeders-Bol, the 2025 World Champion over 400m hurdles, was runner-up to Werro, producing a personal best time (1:57.13s) in her outdoor 800m debut, having switched  from the one-lap hurdles to two laps flat at the end of last year.

“I am super happy with the race,” Broeders-Bol said after. “It is painful in the 800m with all the lactic acid, but also fun. The race went pretty much as expected. I knew Audrey (Werro) was super strong, but she also helped me a lot in the race. I was not even looking for any specific time, but 1:57 is very good.”

There were five personal best in the women’s 800m, and a national record of 1:58.73s for Mauritius’ Rachel Klopfenstein, who came fourth.

That performance rubber-stamps Broeders-Bol’s capabilities ahead of the European Championships in Birmingham this August. There, providing they all navigate the rounds, should be a stellar final between her, Werro and Great Britain’s Keely Hodgkinson — Werro and Hodgkinson are third and sixth on the all-time list thanks to an incredible race at the Stockholm Diamond League earlier this month, while Hodgkinson set an indoor 800m world record earlier this year and beat Werro to win world indoor gold in March.
